page.layout: One text column, full width. Above it, two round medallion engravings (coin portraits) side by side, each with a legend around the rim. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Gathering signature at the bottom right.

main_text.p: CL. TIBERIUS pater Tiberij Cæsaris, Quæstor sub C. Cæsare, Alexandrino bello classi præpositus, plurimum ad victoriam cōtulit: quare & pontifex in locum P. Scipionis substitutus, & ad deducēdas in Galliā colonias, in queis Narbona & Arelate erat, missus est. Cæsare occiso, cunctis turbarum metu abolitione facta: decernentibus, etiā de præmiis tyrānicidarum referendum cēsuit. Tandē indignē ferens nec statim se in conspectum Sexti Pompeij admissum, & fasciūm usu prohibitū, ad M. Antonium traiecit in Achaiam: cum quo breui, reconciliata inter omnes pace, Romam rediit, uxoremq; Liviam Drusillam, & tunc grauidā, & antè iam apud se Tiberium enixam, petenti Augusto concessit: nec multò post diem obiit, utroq; liberorum superstite, Tiberio, Drusoque Neronis. Sueto. in Tiber.

LIVIA Drusilla Cl. Tiberij supradicti uxor, Tiberij imperatoris mater fuit, de qua dictū à nobis est in fine prioris partis huius operis. hanc prægnantem abduxit Augustus: porrò qui cōceptus erat, infans, immaturus est editus: is est Drusus Tiberij Imperatoris frater minor natu, ac Claudij Cæsaris, qui Caligulæ successit, pater: fuit alter Drusus Agrippinæ & Tibe. Impe, filius. Cæterum in osculis Liviæ, & in hac voce defecit Augustus, Livia nostra coniugi memor vive, ac vale.

page.notes: The two medallions are engravings; their rim legends are transcribed as printed text above, with u/v normalised and the partly hidden letters of the right-hand legend (LIVIA. DRVSIL. MAT. TIB. IVN.) read with some doubt. Doubtful: the Q of "Quæstor" has a stroke beneath it in the scan. "Sueto. in Tiber." is a marginal-style reference set within the text line. Running head and page number are as printed.
